narrative.whats_happened:
First technical validation call with Northwind's data platform team. Kenji Watanabe, Head of Data Platform, and Lisa Ferreira, Senior Analytics Engineer, described operational data spread across a warehouse management system, a transportation management system, and telematics feeds from a mixed fleet of owned and contracted carriers. A recent cross-dock delay took most of a day to diagnose and damaged a customer relationship before Northwind's own team understood what had happened.

Marcus walked through Streamline Ingest, Warehouse Native Activation, and Lineage Graph directly against that pain, and resolved five separate technical concerns along the way: whether unification claims would hold up given a bad experience with a prior vendor, whether data of different reliability would get blended without distinction, event ordering for late-arriving carrier updates, whether a missing alert could be diagnosed as easily as a firing one, and alert fatigue from badly-tuned thresholds. One real limitation was conceded and accepted rather than resolved away: the platform won't proactively stop two people from defining conflicting rules.

What's still open is how bad Northwind's cross-system identifier gap actually is. Nobody on the call knew, including Kenji and Lisa themselves, and Lisa agreed to map it before the next call. Kenji positioned himself as the internal advocate for this but was explicit that he doesn't own budget; Northwind's RevOps team, who would, hasn't been looped in yet.

blocking: How bad Northwind's identifier-matching gap actually is, until Lisa's mapping is done. This determines whether the agreed integration approach holds up in practice.
No economic buyer identified yet. RevOps hasn't been brought into the conversation.
not_blocking: No proactive prevention of conflicting rule definitions. Lisa explicitly accepted this as a process problem for her own team, not a product gap.
Whether existing dashboards need rework. Genuinely unresolved but both sides agreed to defer it rather than force an answer without the underlying data.

ae_actions: Send the calendar invite for the follow-up call, targeting roughly two weeks out.
Check in with Kenji on timing for bringing Northwind's RevOps stakeholder into a future call.
Hold off on a specific number until Lisa's mapping clarifies scope; prepare pricing directionally in the meantime.
narrative.sc_loop_close: Five technical concerns got real, resolved answers this call: unification credibility, confidence-tiering across data quality, event ordering, missing-alert diagnosability, and alert fatigue. One limitation, no proactive duplicate-rule prevention, was honestly conceded and Lisa accepted it as a tradeoff rather than a blocker. Nothing technical is currently open except the identifier-matching depth question, and that's explicitly Northwind's mapping exercise to complete, not something for Marcus to resolve.

stakeholders.name: Kenji Watanabe
stakeholders.title: Head of Data Platform
stakeholders.evidence: I can advocate for it, and I think the operational case is strong, but I don't want to represent that I can just greenlight a number the way maybe someone in my exact seat could at a different company.

stakeholders.name: Lisa Ferreira
stakeholders.title: Senior Analytics Engineer
stakeholders.evidence: I'm probably going to be the one actually building and living with whatever we end up doing here.

objections.text: Skepticism that "unification" claims are credible, given a prior vendor's automatic-unification promise turned out to mean nothing
objections.resolution_note: Marcus explained matching logic is deliberate and auditable, not an autonomous black-box; Lisa confirmed this was the most credible answer she could have hoped for.

objections.text: Concern that blending data of different quality/reliability (structured telematics vs. manual carrier updates) would lose the distinction between them
objections.resolution_note: Marcus confirmed source quality/recency is carried alongside the data itself rather than flattened; Lisa accepted this as a good answer with nothing left conceded.

objections.text: Whether out-of-order status updates from slower-reporting carriers get handled correctly
objections.resolution_note: Marcus explained event-time-based resolution with flagging of genuinely suspicious sequences; Lisa called it better thought through than expected.

objections.text: Whether a rule that should have fired but didn't can be diagnosed as easily as one that did fire
objections.resolution_note: Marcus confirmed historical state queries support exactly this case; Lisa said she was glad it wasn't an afterthought.

objections.text: No proactive prevention of two people defining conflicting or duplicate rules
objections.resolution_note: Marcus was direct that this isn't solved by the tooling, only visibility into existing rules is provided; Lisa explicitly accepted this as a process problem for her team rather than a blocker.

objections.text: Risk of alert fatigue from badly-tuned thresholds, similar to muted channels on tools Northwind already runs
objections.resolution_note: Marcus described a shadow-mode tuning approach before alerts reach a human; Lisa said it specifically addressed what she was worried about.

objections.text: Whether existing dashboards can be repointed at the new unified data or need to be rebuilt from scratch

integration_patterns.description: Initial phase scoped to telematics, WMS, and TMS integration via Streamline Ingest, with matching logic against best-available correlating identifiers (shipment number, PO reference, trailer ID); ERP integration deferred to a later phase.
integration_patterns.caveats: Matching logic depth depends on correlating-field coverage across systems, which Northwind hasn't yet mapped. Full identifier-matching viability is unconfirmed pending Lisa's follow-up analysis.

success_criteria.customer_words: It took, I want to say, most of a day to actually piece together why it happened, and by then the customer relationship damage was already done
success_criteria.interpreted: Diagnosing an operational discrepancy currently takes most of a day of cross-team effort; Northwind needs that fast enough to get ahead of the customer, not after the relationship damage is done.

success_criteria.customer_words: our current telematics feed batches every fifteen minutes, so even the "current" position data we're looking at is stale by the time anyone sees it
success_criteria.interpreted: Telematics position data needs to be close to real time, not on a fifteen-minute batch delay.
